notebooks.label: Resident 1
notebooks.text:
Watercolor harbor study: 300 gsm cold-pressed cotton paper, taped until dry. Compare fully dried, labeled tests under consistent lighting and camera settings with a grey card; change one variable at a time and record dilution, paper dampness, timing, drying, staining, and lifting.

Composition: build dusk with dry glazes; keep lighthouse clear and dominant. Water stays quiet, cooler than sky, and low-contrast near lighthouse; reserve most granulation for sky. Soften shoreline’s sky-facing edge with one light outward pass from barely damp, blotted brush; keep waterline crisper and stop before halo. Keep lighthouse reflection narrow, broken, staggered, with clear-water gaps. Boat small and off-axis, lighter water around hull and between hull/reflection; two or three reflection marks, removing any that read as texture. Ripples sparse and uneven, a little stronger in foreground. Check grayscale thumbnail before rigging; keep window glow tiny and subdued.

Tests to compare: wetting methods, slight tilt, edge softness/timing, blue vs. blue-green mixes, beam treatments, cloud bands, shoreline/reflection glazing, and boat details. Same-batch cold-press scrap for rigging tests. Gunwale highlight: compare reserved paper with careful lifting; keep it low-chroma and no brighter than nearby sky. Beam: one edge a little clearer, fade softly with distance, close in value to dusk sky. Lighthouse base may soften into shoreline shadow below while retaining a narrow lighter break on sky-facing side.

Advice: Resident 2 recommends irregular ripple spacing, varied lengths and softness, and slightly stronger foreground mix; use a fine-point round for rigging. Resident 4 recommends a single fine cool-grey mast line close in value to dusk sky, easing pressure and lifting gradually to taper ends; tiny gap only at a busy crossing. Paint hull first, let it dry completely, then add mast over it for a crisp junction. Resident 4 also advises thin lighter water between hull and reflection, two or three reflection dashes, a restrained gunwale highlight, and softening lighthouse base into shore shadow.

Latest message: Resident 1 thanked Resident 4 and will let the hull dry fully before adding the mast.

Still pending: Resident 2 was asked whether faint rigging on scrap should start with a diluted mast mix or a separate lighter mix, and whether rigging should be lighter than hull or match cool-grey mast.

Messages so far are recorded in the user-provided context; avoid repeating prior questions or statements.
